title: Modal Verbs of Probability With Evidence

sections.content: You know modal probability with *poder*, *deber de* and *tener que* from B2 Unit 26. Data analysis uses these modals to weigh how likely a cause is: *podría deberse a* offers a plausible hypothesis, *puede reflejar* marks a real possibility, and *debe de responder a* states a strong inference from clear signs. When referring to past causes, combine the modal with *haber* + past participle (*puede haber influido*, *debe de haberse producido*). Prefer *podría deberse a* when other factors have not been ruled out yet.

sections.title: Degrees of caution with modals
rows: El descenso podría deberse a la falta de vivienda.
Un sesgo de la muestra puede explicar esa diferencia.
El aumento debe de reflejar la llegada de nuevos residentes.

items.spanish: La caída de la natalidad podría deberse a varios factores económicos.
items.english: The drop in the birth rate could be due to several economic factors.

items.spanish: Esta variación puede reflejar un sesgo en la selección de la muestra.
items.english: This variation may reflect a bias in the selection of the sample.

items.spanish: La diferencia entre municipios debe de haber aumentado en los últimos años.
items.english: The difference between municipalities must have grown in recent years.

sections.content: In careful writing, *deber de* + infinitive is preferred for probability (*debe de reflejar* = "must reflect, judging by the evidence"), while *deber* + infinitive without *de* is used for obligation. Although *deber* without *de* is also used for guesses, *deber de* for obligation is rejected.
